ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, and C are on the circle $\odot O$. If $\triangle OAB$ is an equilateral triangle, then what is the measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle OAB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ACB = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB = \frac{1}{2} \times 60^\circ = \boxed{30^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use the central-angle/inscribed-angle theorem. From the image, identify O as the circle center, with segments OA and OB drawn to points A and B on the circle, and ∠ACB formed by chords CA and CB. From the text, triangle OAB is equilateral, so ∠AOB = 60°. Since ∠AOB is the central angle subtending arc AB and ∠ACB is an inscribed angle subtending the same arc AB not containing C, apply the rule that an inscribed angle equals half the corresponding central angle. Therefore ∠ACB = 60° / 2 = 30°.

method.method_draft: Use the chord-length relation via the extended sine rule. From the image, see that triangle ABC is inscribed in the same circle centered at O, and ∠ACB is opposite side AB. From the text, triangle OAB is equilateral, so AB = OA. Since OA is a radius of circle ⊙O, let OA = R; then AB = R. The circumradius of triangle ABC is also R because A, B, and C lie on the circle. By the extended law of sines in triangle ABC, AB = 2R sin(∠ACB). Substitute AB = R to get R = 2R sin(∠ACB), so sin(∠ACB) = 1/2. The image shows ∠ACB is the acute inscribed angle standing on the smaller chord arc AB, so ∠ACB = 30°.
